grammarFocus: 名词性从句入门；that 从句；情态动词与条件表达。
title: The Smart Locker Trial: Privacy, Choices, and Opinions
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。文章和题目均为模拟教学材料，不是真实考试。请根据文章内容作答。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。判断题选择 True、False 或 Not Given。
passage:
A. At Northbridge Community College, a new trial started last month. The college put smart lockers in the library. These lockers open with a student card and a phone app. The college says the lockers save time and stop theft. But some students worry about privacy. They think the lockers collect too much information. The lockers are in the main library, near the entrance. They are blue and have a small screen. Students can use them for free. The college bought 50 lockers for the trial. The trial will last for one year.

B. The smart lockers record when a student opens a locker and which locker they use. The app also asks for a phone number. The college says it needs this data to keep things safe. “We only want to know who is using the lockers and when,” says Mr. Chen, the library manager. “That way, we can find lost items and stop misuse.” However, Mr. Chen admits that the college keeps the data for six months. After that, the college deletes it. The data is stored on a secure computer. Only two staff members can see it. Mr. Chen says the college does not sell the data to other companies.

C. Students have different opinions. “I think it’s a good idea,” says Anna, a first-year student. “I don’t have to carry a heavy bag. The app is easy to use.” But Ben, a second-year student, disagrees. “I don’t like that the college knows my phone number and when I study. It feels like they are watching me.” Other students say they don’t mind, as long as the college explains why it needs the data. Some students also worry that the app might stop working. The college says it will fix any problems quickly.

D. The Student Union held a meeting about the lockers. They invited Mr. Chen and a privacy expert, Dr. Lee. Dr. Lee said, “It is important that students know what data is collected and why. If the college is clear, students can decide if they trust the system.” She also suggested that the college should ask students for permission before sharing data with other companies. Mr. Chen agreed that the college should be more transparent. He promised to put a clear notice next to the lockers. The notice will explain what data is collected and how long it is kept. Dr. Lee also said that students should be able to see their own data. She thinks this will help them feel more confident.

E. The college will decide next month whether to keep the smart lockers. The principal, Ms. Wong, said, “We will listen to students’ opinions. If most students are unhappy, we will change the system or remove it.” The Student Union plans to survey students this week. They will ask questions like: Do you feel safe using the lockers? Do you think the college respects your privacy? The survey will take five minutes. The results will help the college make a decision. Ms. Wong also said that the college will hold a meeting for all students to discuss the trial.

F. In the end, the issue is not just about lockers. It is about how we balance convenience and privacy. As Dr. Lee said, “Technology can help us, but we must ask questions. It is important that we talk about these issues openly.” The college hopes that the trial will teach students to think carefully about technology and their rights. The trial is a chance for everyone to learn. Students can share their ideas with the Student Union. The college wants to hear from as many students as possible.

questions.prompt: What does the college say about the smart lockers?
options: They save time and stop theft.
They are free for all students.
answers: They save time and stop theft.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确提到“The college says the lockers save time and stop theft.”，因此A正确。
questions.evidence: The college says the lockers save time and stop theft.

questions.prompt: How long does the college keep the data?
questions.explanation: 第二段说“the college keeps the data for six months”，所以答案是六个月。
questions.evidence: the college keeps the data for six months

questions.prompt: What is Anna’s opinion about the smart lockers?
options: She thinks they are a good idea.
She thinks they are too expensive.
She thinks they are difficult to use.
answers: She thinks they are a good idea.
questions.explanation: 第三段中Anna说“I think it’s a good idea”，因此选A。
questions.evidence: I think it’s a good idea

questions.prompt: Why does Ben dislike the smart lockers?
options: Because the college knows his phone number and when he studies.
Because the lockers are often broken.
Because he lost his student card.
answers: Because the college knows his phone number and when he studies.
questions.explanation: 第三段中Ben说“I don’t like that the college knows my phone number and when I study.”，所以选A。
questions.evidence: I don’t like that the college knows my phone number and when I study.

questions.prompt: What did Dr. Lee suggest the college should do before sharing data with other companies?
questions.explanation: 第四段中Dr. Lee建议“the college should ask students for permission before sharing data with other companies”，因此选A。
questions.evidence: the college should ask students for permission before sharing data with other companies

questions.prompt: What will the college do next month?
options: Decide whether to keep the smart lockers.
answers: Decide whether to keep the smart lockers.
questions.explanation: 第五段开头说“The college will decide next month whether to keep the smart lockers.”，所以选A。
questions.evidence: The college will decide next month whether to keep the smart lockers.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the main issue discussed?
options: How to balance convenience and privacy.
How to use the library app.
How to become a library manager.
answers: How to balance convenience and privacy.
questions.explanation: 最后一段指出“the issue is not just about lockers. It is about how we balance convenience and privacy.”，因此选A。
questions.evidence: It is about how we balance convenience and privacy.

questions.prompt: The college says it needs the data to keep things ______. (Fill in the blank with ONE word from the passage.)
questions.explanation: 第二段中Mr. Chen说“The college says it needs this data to keep things safe.”，所以填safe。
questions.evidence: The college says it needs this data to keep things safe.

questions.prompt: True or False: The college will definitely keep the smart lockers next month.
questions.explanation: 第五段说“The college will decide next month whether to keep the smart lockers.”，说明还没有决定，因此“will definitely keep”是错误的。
questions.evidence: The college will decide next month whether to keep the smart lockers.

questions.prompt: True or False: Dr. Lee is a teacher at Northbridge Community College.
questions.explanation: 文章只提到Dr. Lee是“a privacy expert”，没有说明她是否是该校教师。因此无法判断，选Not Given。

grammar.title: 名词性从句入门：that 从句与条件表达
grammar.explanation: 英语中，that 从句可以放在动词后作宾语，说明想法、事实或建议。例如：I think that it is a good idea. 这里的 that 可以省略。条件表达常用 if 引导，表示“如果……”。例如：If most students are unhappy, we will change the system. 注意：if 从句用一般现在时，主句用一般将来时。情态动词如 should 表示“应该”，用于提建议。
grammar.example: She also suggested that the college should ask students for permission before sharing data with other companies.

options: I think that the lockers are useful.
I think that the lockers is useful.
I think that are the lockers useful.
I think the lockers are useful that.
answers: I think that the lockers are useful.
questions.explanation: that 从句中主语是 the lockers（复数），谓语用 are。A 选项结构正确。
questions.evidence: I think that the lockers are useful.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: If it ______ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
questions.explanation: if 条件句表示将来时，从句用一般现在时，主句用一般将来时。因此填 rains。
questions.evidence: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a that clause.
options: The teacher said that we should read the notice.
The teacher said that should we read the notice.
The teacher said we should read the notice that.
The teacher said that we should reading the notice.
answers: The teacher said that we should read the notice.
questions.explanation: that 从句用陈述语序，should 后接动词原形。A 选项正确。
questions.evidence: The teacher said that we should read the notice.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: You ______ ask for permission before you use the data.
questions.explanation: 情态动词 should 后直接跟动词原形，不加 to。因此选 should。
questions.evidence: You should ask for permission before you use the data.
